To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
elderly patients with major trauma show a less pronounced decrease in amino acid concentrations than young patients.

the hypoaminoacidemic response of trauma victims is attenuated in elderly patients, who show an increased response in the amino acids arginine and methione, as well as in the ornithine and the citrulline levels.
the elderly have a decreased lean body mass and a decreased protein metabolism response to severe trauma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of major trauma on amino acid concentrations in plasma of geriatric and young patients.
the effect of aging on the metabolic response of geriatric trauma victims.
amino acids and their metabolism in trauma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the amino acid profile in geriatric trauma is different from the profile in young adults.
elderly trauma victims have a decreased plasma amino acid response to injury.
geriatric trauma is associated with a decrease in plasma free amino acids, mainly because of the decrease in nonessential free amino acids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the elderly patients have a lower plasma free amino acid concentration than the young patients.
the elderly are less able to mobilize amino acids from protein reserves and that the response is more variable.
the elderly patients with major trauma have a lower total amino acid concentration than the young ones, but the decrease is not as great as in young trauma.
The main takeaway from our work is that

elderly trauma patients may not be able to mobilize their lean body mass as efficiently as young trauma patients and may therefore be less likely to have the same degree of hypoaminoacidemic response.
elderly patients who suffer trauma are less likely to have a decrease in total free amino acids than younger trauma patients.
older trauma patients have lower plasma free amino acids than young trauma patients, and this difference was more pronounced in young trauma patients than in older trauma patients.
